symbols.name: \operatorname{pa}_{G}(v)
symbols.def: The vertices with a directed edge into \(v\) in \(G\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{bi}_{G}(v)
symbols.def: The bidirected edges of \(G\) incident to \(v\).

symbols.name: \mathcal S_G
symbols.def: \(\mathcal S_G=V\mathbin{\dot\cup}E^{\leftrightarrow}(G)\), with one private source per vertex and one source per bidirected edge.

symbols.name: \mathcal M'
symbols.def: A second model on the same \(G\) and \(\mathcal A\) as \(\mathcal M\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{MIC}}(G,\mathcal A)
symbols.type: normalized marginally informationally complete menu class

symbols.name: \mathcal I_q
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_q=\{(\rho,\boldsymbol b):\rho\in\mathcal R,\ \boldsymbol b\in\prod_{v\in V}\mathcal B_{v,j_v}\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{\mathcal I}
symbols.sig: \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=(q_{\rho}(\boldsymbol b))_{(\rho,\boldsymbol b)\in\mathcal I_q}\)

symbols.name: G_{\mathrm b}
symbols.def: The graph on \(\{X_{\mathrm b},Y_{\mathrm b}\}\) with \(X_{\mathrm b}\to Y_{\mathrm b}\) and \(X_{\mathrm b}\leftrightarrow Y_{\mathrm b}\).

symbols.name: A_{\mathrm b}
symbols.space: A real matrix with rows \(\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\) and columns \((a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\).

symbols.name: B_{\mathcal M,y}
symbols.def: \(B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=W_{\mathcal M}((a_{\mathrm b},y)\mid(z_{\mathrm b},y))\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.space: \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\) with \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\), chosen when \(r_{z^{\circ}}\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.space: \(T\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\times(\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}\times\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}})}\cong\mathbb R^{m^2\times m^2}\).
symbols.def: \(T[(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}),(u_{\mathrm b},z'_{\mathrm b})]=\mathbf 1\{z_{\mathrm b}=z'_{\mathrm b}\}\bigl(\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}/(2m)+1/(2m^2)\bigr)\).

symbols.name: g
symbols.space: \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}\times\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}}\), indexed by \((u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\).
symbols.def: \(g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=2m h(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})-\sum_{a_{\mathrm b}\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}}h(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\), the coordinate formula for \(T^{-1}h\).

symbols.name: B_y^{\sigma}
symbols.sig: \(B_y^{\sigma}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=\sum_{u_{\mathrm b}}m^{-1}f_{X_{\mathrm b}}(a_{\mathrm b}\mid u_{\mathrm b})f_{Y_{\mathrm b}}^{\sigma}(y\mid z_{\mathrm b},u_{\mathrm b})\)

symbols.name: G_{\mathrm f}
symbols.def: The graph has \(X_{\mathrm f}\to M_{\mathrm f}\to Y_{\mathrm f}\) and \(X_{\mathrm f}\leftrightarrow Y_{\mathrm f}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C=(D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{w\},H,G[D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{w\}\mid H])\) has random vertices \(D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{w\}\) and fixed vertices \(H\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{de}_{\mathcal C}(w)
symbols.type: descendant set of the fixing vertex

symbols.name: \operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal C}(S)
symbols.def: The parents in \(\mathcal C\) of a vertex set \(S\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C'
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C'=\phi_w(\mathcal C)\) has random set \(D\) and fixed set \(H\cup\{w\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})
symbols.type: strictly positive algebraic one-fixing certificate set

assumptions.condition: The joint exogenous mass satisfies \(p_{\mathcal M}^{U}(u)=\prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}p_s(u_s)\).

novel.justification: Primitive source positivity is stronger than observed-law positivity and is satisfied by finite latent response-type models after arbitrarily small independent full-support contamination of each source.

assumptions.condition: Every admissible cell of every structural kernel \(f_v\) is strictly positive.

novel.justification: Primitive mechanism positivity is stronger than positivity of the observed law and covers randomized-response, misclassification, and noisy biological transition mechanisms with a positive cell floor.

assumptions.condition: For every \(v\in V\), \(j_v\in\mathcal J_v\), and \(a_v\in\mathcal A_v\), \(\sum_{b_v\in\mathcal B_{v,j_v}}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)=1\).

standard.name: Per-instrument normalization of a separable finite instrument

assumptions.condition: For every \(v\in V\), \(\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{v,\beta_v}:\beta_v\in\mathcal L_v\}=\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_v}\).

standard.name: Marginal informational completeness on the tagged effect family

assumptions.condition: For every \(v\in V\), \(\operatorname{span}\{\psi_{v,\beta_v}:\beta_v\in\mathcal L_v\}=\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_v}\).

standard.name: Marginal informational completeness on the tagged state family

assumptions.condition: For every \(y\in\mathcal A_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\), the joint input-output coordinate \(d_y\) lies in \(\operatorname{span}\{(a_{\mathrm t},z_{\mathrm t})\mapsto\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t}):\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}\).

novel.justification: Joint terminal target-span is satisfied by finite readout devices with one matching state-effect branch \(\phi=\psi=e_y\) per outcome value, including the displayed binary bow menu; it asks only for the diagonal coordinates used by the causal query, not full input-output tomography.

standard.name: Fixable vertex in a conditional ADMG

definitions.name: \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)=\{\mathcal M=((p_s)_{s\in\mathcal S_G},(f_v)_{v\in V}):p_{\mathcal M}^{U}(u)=\prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}p_s(u_s),\ p_s(u_s)>0,\ f_v(a_v\mid z_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u_v,u_{\operatorname{bi}_G(v)})>0\text{ for every admissible cell}\}\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{MIC}}(G,\mathcal A)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{MIC}}(G,\mathcal A)=\{\mathcal I:\sum_{b_v\in\mathcal B_{v,j_v}}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)=1\text{ for every }(v,j_v,a_v),\ \operatorname{span}\{\phi_{v,\beta_v}:\beta_v\in\mathcal L_v\}=\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_v},\ \operatorname{span}\{\psi_{v,\beta_v}:\beta_v\in\mathcal L_v\}=\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_v}\text{ for every }v\in V\}\).

definitions.name: W_{\mathcal M}
definitions.construction: \(W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)=\sum_{u\in\prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}\mathcal U_s}\prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}p_s(u_s)\prod_{v\in V}f_v(a_v\mid z_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u_v,u_{\operatorname{bi}_G(v)})\).

definitions.name: \mathcal E_{\mathcal I}
definitions.construction: \(q_{\rho}(\boldsymbol b)=\sum_{a,z}W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)\prod_{v\in V}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)\psi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(z_v)\), and \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=(q_{\rho}(\boldsymbol b))_{(\rho,\boldsymbol b)\in\mathcal I_q}\).

definitions.name: Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M)
definitions.construction: \(Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{a,z}W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)\mathbf 1\{a_Y=y\}\prod_{v\in X}\mathbf 1\{z_v=x_v\}\prod_{v\notin X}\mathbf 1\{z_v=a_v\}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}=\{\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\}\).

definitions.name: \Theta_{x,y}(q)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{x,y}(q)=\{Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A),\ \mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=q\}\).

definitions.name: \operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{x,y})
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{x,y})\Longleftrightarrow[\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M')\Rightarrow Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M')]\) for every \(\mathcal M,\mathcal M'\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\).

definitions.name: \lambda^y
definitions.construction: Choose \(\lambda^y\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\) satisfying \(\sum_{\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\lambda^y_{\beta_Y}\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t})=d_y(a_{\mathrm t},z_{\mathrm t})=\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm t}=y,\ z_{\mathrm t}=y\}\) for every \(a_{\mathrm t},z_{\mathrm t}\in\mathcal A_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\); a second admissible choice \(\widetilde\lambda^y\) satisfies the same coordinate equations.

definitions.name: q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\lambda^y)
definitions.construction: \(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\lambda^y)=\sum_{\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\lambda^y_{\beta_Y}\bar q_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}\), where \(\bar q_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}=q_{(j_X,j_Y)}(b_X,b_Y)\) for \(\beta_X=(j_X,b_X)\) and \(\beta_Y=(j_Y,b_Y)\).

definitions.name: A_{\mathrm b}
definitions.construction: \(A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]=\phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(a_{\mathrm b})\psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(z_{\mathrm b})\) for \(\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\) and \((a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\).

definitions.name: r_{z^{\circ}}
definitions.construction: \(r_{z^{\circ}}[a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}]=\mathbf 1\{z_{\mathrm b}=z^{\circ}\}\) for \((a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\).

definitions.name: (\mathcal M_h^{+},\mathcal M_h^{-})
definitions.construction: Choose \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\) with \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\), identify the shared-edge alphabet with \(\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}\), and set \(p(u_{\mathrm b})=1/m\). Give all private sources one state. In both models set \(f_{X_{\mathrm b}}(a_{\mathrm b}\mid u_{\mathrm b})=\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}/2+1/(2m)\). With \(T[(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}),(u_{\mathrm b},z'_{\mathrm b})]=\mathbf 1\{z_{\mathrm b}=z'_{\mathrm b}\}(\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}/(2m)+1/(2m^2))\), set \(g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=2m h(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})-\sum_{a_{\mathrm b}}h(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\), \(L=\lVert g\rVert_{\infty}\), and \(t=1/(2kL)\). Choose \(y^{\dagger}\ne y\). For \(\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}\), define \(f^{\sigma}_{Y_{\mathrm b}}(\ell\mid z_{\mathrm b},u_{\mathrm b})=1/k+\sigma t g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\) when \(\ell=y\), \(1/k-\sigma t g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\) when \(\ell=y^{\dagger}\), and \(1/k\) otherwise; \(\mathcal M_h^{\sigma}\) is the bow SCM with these source masses and node kernels.

definitions.name: \mathcal I_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}
definitions.construction: At \(X_{\mathrm b}\), use three instruments: a one-branch instrument \((\phi,\psi)=(\mathbf 1,\psi^{+})\), a one-branch instrument \((\mathbf 1,\psi^{-})\), and a two-branch instrument \((e_0,\psi^{+}),(e_1,\psi^{+})\). At \(Y_{\mathrm b}\), use the two-branch instrument \((e_0,e_0),(e_1,e_1)\). Thus \(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}\) has rows \(\mathbf 1\otimes\psi^{+},\mathbf 1\otimes\psi^{-},e_0\otimes\psi^{+},e_1\otimes\psi^{+}\).

definitions.name: (G_{\mathrm f},K_{\mathrm f},q_{\mathrm f},P_{\mathrm f})
definitions.construction: Use \(G_{\mathrm f}\), \(K_{\mathrm f}=\begin{pmatrix}3/4&1/4\\1/4&3/4\end{pmatrix}\), and \((q_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},0),q_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},1))=(33,15),(7,9),(9,7),(15,33)\) divided by \(128\), in \((x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f})=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) order. Define each pair \((P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},0),P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},1))\) by left multiplication with \((K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\).

definitions.name: R_{\mathcal C}
definitions.construction: Fix every coefficient \(R_{\mathcal C}[\eta,i]\in\mathbb R\), for \(\eta\in\mathcal I_{\mathcal C}\) and \(i\in\mathcal I_q\), and set \(k_{\mathcal C}(q)_\eta=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_q}R_{\mathcal C}[\eta,i]q_i\).

definitions.name: (U_w,V_w)
definitions.construction: For \(\eta=(a_D,a_w,a_H)\in\mathcal I_{\mathcal C}\), set \(U_w[(a_w,a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H),\eta]=\mathbf 1\{\eta\text{ agrees on }(a_w,a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H)\}\) and \(V_w[(a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H),\eta]=\mathbf 1\{\eta\text{ agrees on }(a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H)\}\). Matrix multiplication therefore performs exactly the two displayed marginalizations.

definitions.name: \Phi_w
definitions.construction: For \(\xi=(a_D,a_H,a_w)\in\mathcal I_D\), \(\eta=(a_D,a_w,a_H)\), and \(h=(a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H)\), define \(\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})_\xi=k_{\mathcal C,\eta}(V_wk_{\mathcal C})_h/(U_wk_{\mathcal C})_{(a_w,h)}\).

definitions.name: (N_D,O_D,S_D)
definitions.construction: Set \(N_D[(a_H,a_w),(a_D',a_H',a_w')]=\mathbf 1\{(a_H,a_w)=(a_H',a_w')\}\). Fix a finite explicit list \(\Omega_D\) of retained overlap rows; for each \(r\in\Omega_D\), record its stated district-cell coefficients as \(O_D[r,\xi]\) and its stated accessible-coordinate coefficients as \(S_D[r,i]\), so the complete retained contract is the coordinate equality \(\sum_{\xi\in\mathcal I_D}O_D[r,\xi]\kappa_D(\xi)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_q}S_D[r,i]q_i\) for every \(r\in\Omega_D\).

definitions.name: \mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})=\{\kappa_D\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_D}:k_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star})>0,\ U_wk_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star})>0,\ \kappa_D=\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star}))>0,\ N_D\kappa_D=\mathbf 1,\ O_D\kappa_D=S_Dq^{\star}\}\).

definitions.name: \mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}
definitions.construction: Apply source splitting to the positive table \(k_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star})\), formulate the required private-source and per-bidirected-edge masses as a product-constrained transportation polytope, and seek a rational interior point whose contractions are \(q^{\star}\) and whose coordinate fixing image is \(\kappa_D\), while holding every observed-node table \(f_v\) common across the two models.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\) and normalized separable menu \(\mathcal I\), every accessible branch law equals its coordinate in \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)\), and every atomic intervention query equals the displayed contraction of the same \(W_{\mathcal M}\).
statements.justification: The reduction supplies a single finite tensor on which both the probe coordinates and the intervention target are linear contractions.
statements.gap: Friend et al. use local process contractions for Markovian models; this lemma fixes the independent edge-source ADMG semantics needed for the bow and one-step contracts.
statements.consumer: Every bow oracle and the Ananke coordinate backend use this common tensor interface.

statements.statement: Under joint terminal target-span, every admissible \(\lambda^y\) satisfies the pointwise sanity reduction \(\sum_{\beta_Y}\lambda^y_{\beta_Y}\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t})=\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm t}=y,\ z_{\mathrm t}=y\}\). Consequently, for every attainable bow tensor, \(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\lambda^y)=\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\) and \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}r_{z^{\circ}}[a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}]B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\). If \(\lambda^y\) and \(\widetilde\lambda^y\) both satisfy the synthesis equations, their responses coincide; the common coordinate is denoted \(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\).
statements.justification: Terminal recovery must be a property of the probe tensor, not of an arbitrary dual frame.
statements.gap: Friend et al. use dual frames inside mechanism recovery; this lemma isolates the diagonal input-output coordinate and its exact synthesis invariance for the latent bow oracle.
statements.consumer: Ananke may choose any numerically stable terminal dual without changing the synthesized response vector.

statements.statement: The operator \(T\) is an invertible \(m^2\)-by-\(m^2\) block-diagonal matrix, with one block \(I/(2m)+\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}/(2m^2)\) for each \(z_{\mathrm b}\), and its inverse block is \(2mI-\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\). Therefore the explicit coordinate definition of \(g\) satisfies \(Tg=h\), so \(L>0\), and \(B_y^{+}-B_y^{-}=2th\). For every branch pair, \([\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M_h^{+})]_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}-[\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M_h^{-})]_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}=2t(A_{\mathrm b}h)_{\beta_X}[\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y)-\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y^{\dagger})]=0\), whereas \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^{+})-Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^{-})=2t r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\).
statements.justification: This calculation makes the repaired dimensions and the exact evidence-null and query-separation identities auditable coordinate by coordinate.
statements.gap: Existing hedge constructions do not provide this typed \(m^2\)-coordinate disturbing-probe cancellation identity.
statements.consumer: Ananke can verify a failed bow certificate using two matrix products and the displayed nonzero scalar.

statements.statement: In \(G_{\mathrm b}\), if \(r_{z^{\circ}}\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\), choose \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\) with \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\). The construction \((\mathcal M_h^{+},\mathcal M_h^{-})\) gives two members of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G_{\mathrm b},\mathcal A)\) with identical \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}\), unequal \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}\), exactly \(m\) states for the shared edge source, and primitive cell floor at least \(1/(2\max\{m,k\})\).
statements.justification: The failure witness is an interior pair of legal edge-source SCMs, not a signed array outside the causal model.
statements.gap: Shpitser and Pearl give passive-law hedge twins, while Kivva et al. treat observed-law positivity; neither construction preserves arbitrary disturbing-probe contractions under primitive positivity.
statements.consumer: This pair is Ananke's exact negative certificate for every failed bow row-span test.

statements.statement: For an attainable bow tensor, if \(c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=\widetilde c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}\), then \(\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)=\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}\widetilde c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\).
statements.justification: The bow functional must not depend on which treatment-side row-span coefficients are selected.
statements.gap: Standard frame reconstruction gives coefficient invariance for full tomography; this lemma proves it only for the query-relevant bow row space.
statements.consumer: Ananke can change linear solvers or generalized inverses without changing the returned causal value.

statements.statement: For \(G_{\mathrm b}\), arbitrary normalized separable probes at \(X_{\mathrm b}\), and a terminal menu at \(Y_{\mathrm b}\) satisfying joint terminal target-span, \(\operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{z^{\circ},y})\) holds if and only if \(r_{z^{\circ}}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\). On success, any \(c\) satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}\) gives the terminal-synthesis- and coefficient-invariant functional \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}=\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\). On failure, the positive-twin lemma gives one attainable common fiber with unequal query values.
statements.justification: This is the exact class-wide identification frontier for the smallest latent district.
statements.gap: Friend et al. prove Markovian mechanism recovery under MIC; the latent bow instead has a query-specific row-span equivalence with an explicit primitive-positive common-fiber converse.
statements.consumer: Ananke obtains a complete constant-size oracle returning either a functional or executable positive twins.

statements.statement: If \(m=k=2\), the terminal menu at \(Y_{\mathrm b}\) satisfies joint terminal target-span, and \(X_{\mathrm b}\) has one two-branch instrument whose two effects and two states are each linearly independent, then \(r_0,r_1\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\). Both binary bow intervention responses fail global identification although the treatment instrument is marginally informationally complete.
statements.justification: The symbolic obstruction replaces the finite enumeration of minimal binary menus.
statements.gap: The Markovian MIC theorem does not provide a latent-bow necessity result for a single minimal instrument.
statements.consumer: This proposition supplies the smallest negative menu regression test for Ananke.

statements.statement: For \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}\), normalization holds separately for each of the three \(X_{\mathrm b}\) instruments, the effect and state spans over \(\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\) are both \(\mathbb R^2\), and the matching terminal branches satisfy \(e_0\otimes e_0=d_0\) and \(e_1\otimes e_1=d_1\). The treatment rows give \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})=3<4\), while \(r_0,r_1\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})\). Hence both binary intervention responses are globally identified on the latent bow although full branch-map tomography is impossible. This establishes query-specific identification in a latent-confounded bow regime using a non-tomographic disturbing-probe menu; Friend et al.'s Markovian mechanism-recovery theorem supplies the instrument framework but is not claimed to be contained or tightened.
statements.justification: The explicit menu separates query identification from both marginal completeness alone and four-dimensional process tomography.
statements.gap: Friend et al., Theorem 1, recovers whole mechanisms on Markovian graphs under MIC; this theorem recovers both intervention responses on a latent-confounded bow from a non-tomographic three-dimensional branch span.
statements.consumer: The four explicit treatment rows form Ananke's positive bow fixture adjacent to the minimal-menu failure fixture.

statements.statement: For the indexed tensor \(q_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},b_{\mathrm f})\), applying \((K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}3/2&-1/2\\-1/2&3/2\end{pmatrix}\) to each \((x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f})\)-slice reconstructs \((P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},0),P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},1))=(42,6),(6,10),(10,6),(6,42)\) divided by \(128\), in \((x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f})=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) order. The ordinary front-door functional then equals \(3/8\) under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=0)\) and \(5/8\) under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=1)\).
statements.justification: The complete eight-cell table fixes the tensor ordering and checks that signed terminal inversion remains inside the probability simplex in this legal fixture.
statements.gap: Ordinary front-door identification starts from a passive law; this calculation reconstructs that law from explicitly indexed disturbing mediator-probe coordinates.
statements.consumer: The eight rational cells and two exact targets provide an end-to-end Ananke arithmetic test.

statements.statement: Let \(w\) be fixable in \(\mathcal C\). If \(k_{\mathcal C}\) is a strictly positive normalized kernel on \(D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{w\}\) given \(H\), then the coordinate formula \(\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})\) is strictly positive and satisfies \(N_D\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})=\mathbf 1\). Moreover the formula is exactly the ordinary one-step fixing quotient by the conditional mass of \(w\) given \(\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)\) and \(H\).
statements.justification: This proposition verifies the exact algebra performed before any causal lift is claimed.
statements.gap: Richardson et al. define fixing for a kernel already supplied by a passive law; this result isolates the coordinate quotient used for a probe-reconstructed candidate.
statements.consumer: Ananke can validate positivity and normalization of a proposed one-step certificate without invoking an SCM solver.

statements.statement: Determine whether every \(q^{\star}\in\mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}\) and every \(\kappa_D\in\mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})\) admit a shared-mechanism independent-edge-source lift: construct \(\mathcal M,\mathcal M'\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\) with \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M')=q^{\star}\), identical observed-node tables \((f_v)_{v\in V}\), mutually independent private and per-bidirected-edge sources, and one-step fixed district kernel of \(\mathcal M'\) equal to \(\kappa_D\); or characterize, by an additional explicit algebraic equality, the smallest obstruction inside \(\mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})\). Any positive result must give a finite latent-support bound and a primitive positivity floor in terms of the graph, alphabets, and displayed matrices.
statements.justification: This is the exact unresolved local-to-causal step; keeping it open prevents algebraic normalization from being mistaken for an edge-source SCM realization.
statements.gap: Richardson et al. begin with a passive-law kernel, and finite response-type programs do not preserve both shared observed mechanisms and independent per-edge sources across disturbing-probe fibers.
statements.consumer: A positive lift gives Ananke a sound first district step; a minimal algebraic obstruction tells the compiler exactly which extra certificate to check.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite menu of known separable local probe kernels, with branch effects normalized separately within each instrument label.
sampling_model.units: The proposal's identification claims concern exact accessible regime probabilities; empirical sampling is outside the frozen bow and one-fixing scope.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal target is \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), which need not coincide with an accessible probe regime.
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive source mass and every structural-kernel cell is strictly positive, a condition stronger than positivity of the induced observed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The local probe states and effects are known; no nuisance estimator is introduced in this discovery core.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 recovers every mechanism in a Markovian causal model when each local instrument is marginally informationally complete.
Sections 2--4 define legal fixing and intrinsic kernels starting from a supplied passive-law kernel.
The ID algorithm is sound and complete for passive observational input, with a hedge witnessing nonidentification.
General identifiability under observed-law positivity requires positivity-aware failure constructions.
Finite discrete causal compatibility can be encoded as polynomial optimization over canonical response functions.
The front-door criterion identifies an intervention distribution from a compatible passive observed law.

tldr: Known disturbing probes reveal contractions of both input and output ports, not a passive observed law. On the primitive-positive canonical edge-source bow with joint terminal target-span, global identification is exactly a treatment-branch row-span condition: success yields a terminal-synthesis- and coefficient-invariant arithmetic functional, while failure yields strictly positive same-evidence twins through an explicit invertible \(m^2\)-coordinate operator and an \(m\)-state shared source. An explicit marginally complete three-instrument menu has only a three-dimensional treatment branch span, has matching terminal input-output branches, and identifies both bow responses, giving a query-identification result in a latent-confounded regime distinct from Markovian mechanism recovery. Beyond the bow, the scope stops after one legal CADMG fixing step: every reconstruction, conditional quotient, normalization row, and retained overlap is written as a finite matrix contract, and the genuinely causal independent-edge-source lift from the strictly positive algebraic certificate is exposed as the open question.

project_justification.gap: Friend et al. recover mechanisms from marginally complete disturbing instruments in the Markovian regime, while ordinary ADMG fixing starts from an already valid passive-law kernel. Neither addresses the distinct problem of query identification on a latent bow or shows that a positive normalized array reconstructed from disturbing-probe coordinates is induced by independent per-edge sources.
project_justification.niche: Within the primitive-positive latent-bow regime, the project identifies the query-specific row-span frontier between marginal completeness alone and full split-port tomography, and at the first legal fixing step isolates a precise algebraic-versus-causal realizability gap.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the exact bow row-span equivalence under an explicit joint terminal target-span condition, invariant synthesis, dimensionally explicit bounded positive twins, and the non-tomographic positive menu; it then isolates one coordinate-level fixing certificate and the shared-mechanism edge-source lift as the sole open construction.

related_work: Friend, Kissinger, Spekkens, and Wolfe (2025, Definitions 8--9, Proposition 6, and Theorem 1) formalize separable disturbing instruments and recover Markovian mechanisms under marginal informational completeness. The present binary-bow theorem studies a different latent-confounded graph and query target, using that instrument framework as motivation: both bow intervention responses are recovered from a three-dimensional branch span although full four-dimensional branch-map tomography fails; no theorem-class containment or tightening of Friend et al. is claimed. Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (2023, Sections 2--4) define fixability and kernel fixing when a passive-law kernel is already available; the coordinate proposition reduces exactly to their one-step quotient, whereas causal realization of a probe-reconstructed algebraic certificate is left open. Shpitser and Pearl (2006, Theorems 1--2) inform the common-fiber witness benchmark, and Kivva et al. (2022) inform the insistence on positive failure constructions; neither is claimed to establish primitive-positive disturbing-probe twins. Duarte et al. (2024) and Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022) inform finite response-type and support-reduction techniques, but they do not supply shared observed mechanisms with mutually independent per-bidirected-edge sources. Pearl (1995) supplies the ordinary front-door endpoint checked by the explicit eight-cell reconstruction. Full branch-map tomography is treated only as standard finite-dimensional boundary infrastructure.
technical_internal_limitation: The equalities defining the algebraic set use only finite vectors and matrices. Positivity, normalization, and all listed overlaps do not by themselves certify membership in the canonical independent-edge-source SCM class. The source-product and shared-mechanism lift is therefore not asserted by the certificate or by the coordinate fixing proposition.
honest_scope: The finite claims are the bow row-span equivalence under joint terminal target-span, its two independent dual-invariance lemmas, the typed positive-twin cancellation identity, the explicit positive twins, the minimal-menu obstruction, the three-instrument query separation, the rational front-door check, and positivity and normalization of one coordinate fixing quotient. The matching binary terminal branches reduce exactly to \(e_0\otimes e_0=d_0\) and \(e_1\otimes e_1=d_1\); the front-door fixture reduces to the eight cells \((42,6;6,10;10,6;6,42)/128\) and targets \(3/8,5/8\). The shared-mechanism independent-edge-source lift from the algebraic one-step certificate, including a finite latent-support bound or a smallest extra algebraic obstruction, is open. No all-ADMG recursive calculus, complexity theorem, or inference theorem is claimed. Under passive observation, the coordinate map reduces to the ordinary one-step fixing quotient; under a full branch span, standard tomography remains a boundary case rather than a contribution.
